content.title: Cleveland Guardians TV schedule 2026: How to watch today, stream games live for free
content.text: CLEVELAND, Ohio -- Guardians baseball is finally back! Jose Ramirez and Steven Kwan spearhead a youthful bunch backed by a seasoned pitching staff looking for a deep push into October. Find out how to watch Cleveland Guardians baseball for free during the 2026 season. How do I watch Cleveland Guardians games for free? Cleveland Guardians baseball will once again be available on multiple streaming services. You can watch Guardians games at no cost with a free trial from DIRECTV, which also offers $35 off your first month. FuboTV also offers a free trial and $25 off your first month. MLB will continue to produce and stream Guardians games on TV for the 2026 baseball season through their direct-to-consumer streaming option for Guardians fans – CLEGuardians.TV. The trio of Matt Underwood, Rick Manning and on-field reporter Andre Knott will return for their 12th consecutive year, anchoring local Guardians TV games in the booth.CLEGuardians.TV will have a 30-minute pregame show for all home games (no pregame shows for road games) and will have a 15-minute postgame show for all games.The Guardians also extended their longstanding partnership with WKYC, Cleveland’s local NBC affiliate, who will simulcast 10 games produced by Guardians TV throughout the regular season; these 10 games will also be available locally in the markets of Columbus, Toledo, Erie (PA), Buffalo (NY) and Charleston-Huntington (WV). WKYC will air an 11th nationally televised game featuring the Guardians on April 12 against the Atlanta Braves as part of NBC’s Sunday Night Baseball.In total, the Guardians will have 13 nationally televised games: (NBC: 1, Peacock: 3, FOX: 5, FS1: 3, TBS: 1, ESPN: TBA, Apple TV+: TBA).Guardians TV Streaming guideWhat happened last year? Stephen Vogt became the first skipper to win Manager of the Year in his first two seasons as the Guardians orchestrated a historic 15.5-game comeback to snatch the American League Central away from the Detroit Tigers down the home stretch of the regular season. It marked their second consecutive Central crown. The thrilling regular season conclusion was met with a bitter postseason end in Game 3 against the Tigers in the AL Wild Card round.Despite the loss, Cleveland can always relish a picturesque Autumn afternoon where it completed the greatest division comeback in MLB history after Brayan Rocchio hit a three-run, walk-off home run to lift the Guardians over the Tigers, 9-8, in the 10th inning, clinching the division title. Cleveland Guardians designated hitter Jose Ramirez waves a AL Central Champions flag after defeating the Texas Rangers 9-8 in the tenth inning. A preview of the 2026 Cleveland Guardians After chasing down the Tigers in the regular season, the blueprint to a third-straight division title is on the table. One of the worst offenses in baseball needs reinforcements after batting a franchise-low .226 and ranking 28th in runs scored in MLB. Offense in desperate need of helpCleveland staples Jose Ramirez, fresh off his seven-year, $175 million extension, and Steven Kwan, who was almost flipped at last year’s trade deadline, will again anchor the bewildered offense that did just enough to sneak into the postseason last year. Kyle Manzardo, Brayan Rocchio and Chase DeLauter are names to watch in 2026. The question remains whether the front office will finally address Cleveland’s glaring weakness? Six starting pitchers, five spots Starting pitchers Gavin Williams and Tanner Bibee headline a deep starting rotation as Slade Cecconi, Joey Cantillo and Parker Messick provide no shortage of firepower on the mound. Messick won the final starting spot. Logan Allen, who struggled in the spring, was the odd man out and will begin the season in the minor leagues. A tangled web and one of baseball’s best bullpens Flamethrowing closer Emmanuel Clase and starting pitcher Louis L. Ortiz remain away from the team as they navigate a tangled web of baseball gambling allegations. Clase, the franchise save leader, is under indictment from federal prosecutors and is still owed $6.4 million from the club. Both were moved to unpaid, non-disciplinary leave effective March 20, while awaiting a November trial. The Guardians have stuffed the back half of one of the best bullpens in baseball over the last two years. Cade Smith returns along with Tim Herrin, Matt Festa and Erik Sabrowski. Smith will be the primary closer after dabbling in the role in 2025. Hunter Gaddis, a staple in the bullpen, will open the season on the injured list as he deals with a right forearm strain. A brutal opening slateThe Guardians will face a brutal schedule to open up the season, opening with a four-game series against the ALCS finalist Seattle Mariners before battling the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers. Cleveland plays its home opener on April 3 against the Chicago Cubs, part of a three-game series. The Guardians get their first look at the American League champion Toronto Blue Jays on April 24, part of a three-game series. Guards ball Cleveland continues to defy the odds of baseball’s version of a minuscule payroll (projected $74 million) and have won six AL Central titles in the last 10 years, including a World Series berth in 2016 and trip to the ALCS in 2024. The franchise has topped two million in attendance for the last two years. A powerful pitching staff and timely at-bats that do just enough to reach the playoff threshold have been the norm at the corner of Carnegie and Ontario for quite some time. Will it be the same old song and dance in 2026? Where can I watch Cleveland Guardians games out of market? MLB.TV has access to every out-of-market game live and on demand. FuboTV subscribers can add MLB.TV to their plan starting at $24.99 per month to receive 30 individual team feeds and MLB Big Inning. Archived games are also available on-demand for 72 hours.What is FuboTV?FuboTV, which features a free trial and $25 off the first month, offers more than 400 live channels with an emphasis on live sports. It offers a $64.99 base plan. The service comes with 1,000 hours of DVR space and streams on most devices.What is DIRECTV?DIRECTV’s streaming service, which has a five-day free trial and $35 off your first month, is one of the most flexible options available, offering three tiers of programming to suit your needs and budget. The Choice Plan, available starting at $89.99 per month, offers 105+ channels, plus unlimited DVR storage and thousands of on-demand titles.What is Sling?Sling TV users can now get a Day Pass for $4.99, Weekend Pass for $9.99, Week Pass for $14.99, Monthly Pass for $45.99 and Season Pass for $199.99 for the first five months and $45.99 per month thereafter. You can also subscribe to either the Blue package or the Orange package depending on your viewing preferences. Sling Blue allows up to three streams at a time and Sling Orange allows one stream at a time. Both the Blue and Orange packages are $23 for the first month, then increase to $45.99 per month thereafter.What is Peacock? Peacock offers multiple sports coverage on select games, including MLB, NBA, NFL, Big Ten football, Premier League soccer, PGA Tour and more. Catch all the action for $10.99 per month or $109.99 annually. This service also features movies and hit television shows, as well as current NBC programming.
